hypothesis: The canonical exact fixed-support ternary bitstream can be packed and unpacked on one x86 CPU core at at least 20 million Qwen-shaped weights per second with exact code recovery and no more than 1.48 raw code bits per weight

scope.claim_boundary: native load-time codec only; not a fused GEMV, token-throughput, model-quality, semi-lossless, or breakthrough result

representation.ordering: lexicographic support rank with support-ordered signs in the low bits
representation.bitstream: fixed-width group codes concatenated least-significant-bit first with zero terminal padding
representation.binomial_table: thread-safe one-time Pascal table for n 0 through 128 and canonical k 0 through 64; process metadata only
representation.decode_target: dense signed int8 ternary codes for load-time validation

measurement.compiler: system C compiler with C11 O3 Wall Wextra Werror shared PIC and mtune=native
measurement.threading: one process pinned to one physical CPU; codec itself is single-threaded
measurement.timed_path: safe C ABI with preallocated input payload and output buffers
measurement.full_model_projection: diagnostic only; divide 27,781,427,952 weights by observed one-core throughput

promotion_rules: a pass establishes only exact native load-time coding at the frozen x86 floor
raw code bits exclude scales correction retained tensors metadata and alignment, which remain in the complete model ledger
Pascal-table process metadata is not model storage but must be disclosed
on-the-fly inference requires a separately preregistered fused compressed GEMV and cannot be inferred from dense decode throughput
infrastructure-invalid work is neither a zero nor a completed result
Qwen 4B compute is forbidden in this research lane
this benchmark cannot establish semi-lossless compression or a scientific breakthrough
